_meta.description: Golden validation for the RECAP theme-coverage judge (eval_recap_judge). Unlike the why-judge's binary filler label, RECAP's binary 'clean' is DEGENERATE -- compressing ~300 titles into 3 sentences makes EVERY recap drop a prominent theme, so defect-rate is ~100% for both models and a clean/defective agreement number is uninformative. The meaningful validation is THEME-LEVEL PRECISION: of the themes the judge flags as 'missed', what fraction are real prominent omissions (verifiable against the window's title frequencies + the recap text) vs nitpicks (e.g. editorially-filtered entertainment the digest is SUPPOSED to skip).
_meta.method: Independent human audit (label_real) of every theme the judge flagged across 4 windows / 8 recaps, cross-referenced against eval_recap_windows.theme_frequencies and the recap text. Judge verdicts cached from data/recap_ab.json (sonnet-4-6, 2026-06-24 run).

findings.missed_theme_precision: ~0.94 -- flagged misses are almost always real prominent omissions
findings.fabrication_precision: 1.0 on the single flagged case -- caught a real subtle Haiku error (claimed oil 'rallied' on the Iran deal when titles say oil slid; Sonnet got it right)
known_flaws: Nitpick: counts editorially-filtered topics (Oscars/entertainment) as 'missed major themes' by title-frequency, though the digest's SELECT tier deliberately filters them -- a symmetric ~1-count inflation per recap.

Noise/recall inconsistency: in 2026-06-15 it flagged Khamenei's death (11 titles) as missed for Sonnet but NOT for Haiku, though both omitted it. Absolute counts carry +/-1-2 error; trust the PAIRED direction, not precise counts.
findings.decision_use: Judge precision is high enough that the paired missed-theme comparison is meaningful (read as 'Haiku ~= Sonnet', not a precise ranking). Recall noise means small count gaps are not significant.
